newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy seen issuing 12.5 trln lire BOTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy seen issuing 12.5 trln lire BOTs.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected to issue 11.75 trillion to 13 trillion lire of short term bills (BOT) at its next auction, for an average of 12.5 trillion lire, against 14.75 trillion maturing, a Reuter poll showed.
The Treasury is also expected to issue two trillion lire of 18-month zero coupon certificates (CTZ) and 2.5 trillion lire of a new 24-month CTZ maturing on March 15, 1999.
On Thursday March 6 it will detail the amounts it will offer at the March 11 auction. Settlement is on March 14.
Analysts said the Treasury would tend to favour issuing more 24 month CTZ than the 18 month paper because the yield curve is currently flat and it will therefore try to lengthen maturities.
Analysts do not see any particular change in the Treasury's issuance policy and all agree that it will issue less BOTs than are maturing.
